page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.r7.4xlarge demonstrates consistent mid-range performance. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 9464.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 20751.25. Memory performance is highlighted by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 849.57 GB/sec, though uncached large block read bandwidth drops to 102.07 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance processes 15.46 million Redis SET operations per second. However, performance tradeoffs are evident in complex workloads; while small 135M LLM inference is handled efficiently, prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model drops to a weak 30.95 tokens/second.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is rooted in its high memory density, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable compute performance without resource contention. This profile is highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and moderate data processing tasks.
